summary: Intermittent long-tail request delays caused by soft 429 enforcement window amplified by synchronized client retries
description:
Issue summary: Several customer requests from ScribeHealth during production traffic windows observed long-tail delays (10s-60s) or client-level timeouts. Customer reports intermittent failures while other requests succeed.

Impact: A subset (~0.5-1%) of requests for this customer see token-generation stalls that surface to the client as streaming pauses or total request timeouts. Affects critical clinical summarization flows; customer reported user-facing errors and elevated error rates in their dashboards.

Timeline (local):
- 2026-03-10T09:12Z: First alert from ScribeHealth via support chat (#support).
- 2026-03-10T09:20Z: Support triaged to SRE, initial sample traces requested.
- 2026-03-10T09:35Z: Observed bursts of 429s and elevated queue depths in rate-limiter metrics concurrent with customer retry spikes.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Send high-concurrency streaming requests using SDK v1.12 with default retry/backoff.
2) Observe occasional stream stalls after initial tokens and increased 302/timeout events on client side during 2x-3x traffic bursts.

Observed behavior:
- Server returns soft-429 enforcement in short windows (rate-limiter queueing) rather than hard rejection for some requests; these are exposed as delayed token emission.
- Customer SDK retries are synchronized (no jitter) causing fanout that deepens the queue and increases per-request latency in the window.
- Traces show request accepted by gateway, then waits in rate-limiter queue (approx 200ms-4s) then forwarded; a minority experience multi-second queueing (10s+).

Initial hypothesis: Short soft-throttle windows (burst enforcement with in-memory queueing) combined with client SDKs that retry quickly and in lockstep cause amplification. The amplification pushes requests into longer queue positions producing long-tail latency perceived as timeouts.
investigation_notes: Checked api-gateway logs (prod/us-east-1) for sample request IDs; spike window matches customer reported times: 2026-03-10T09:30:00Z-09:38:00Z
Rate-limiter dashboard: token_drain_time and queue_depth metrics show brief spikes; 95th->99.9th percentile drift during window
Serving-runtime traces show most model backends healthy; no model OOMs or kernel errors found
Collected SDK telemetry from ScribeHealth: SDK v1.12 default retry policy retries immediately with linear backoff; no jitter set
Correlation: customer concurrency increased by ~2.8x when their autoscaling launched a batch worker; synchronized startup likely caused initial burst
Sample request IDs: req_20260310_us-3749a, req_20260310_us-3753f, req_20260310_us-3771d (attached logs)
Confirmed similar pattern in internal synthetic load test when running many identical clients without jitter

root_cause: Short-duration soft 429 enforcement windows combined with synchronized client retries (no jitter) amplified incoming burst, causing elevated queueing and long-tail latency for a small percentage of requests.
resolution:
Immediate workaround provided to customer: enable randomized exponential backoff (SDK v1.12 config) and throttle client concurrency during peak bursts. Applied temporary quota bump for ScribeHealth to reduce immediate queuing.

Planned fix: rollout server-side soft-throttle debounce and reduce max queue hold time for burst windows; add metrics and alerting to detect synchronized retry patterns. Patch PR: github.com/redwood/inference-runtime/pull/4482.

Postmortem actions: update SDK quickstart to recommend jitter, add a runbook entry on retry-amplification, and create an automated detector for synchronized retries tied to customer-level alerts.
